summary: Amorolfine is a topical morpholine antifungal applied as a 5% medicated nail lacquer for the treatment of mild distal/lateral onychomycosis not involving the nail matrix (lunula). It has broad activity against dermatophytes, yeasts, and some moulds by disrupting fungal cell membrane ergosterol synthesis. Treatment is prolonged (months) until a healthy nail regrows. It is not FDA-approved; information reflects EMA/SmPC and BNF sources.
indications: Treatment of mild onychomycosis (fungal nail infection) caused by dermatophytes, yeasts, and moulds, affecting up to two nails and not involving the nail matrix
Some formulations are used for dermatomycoses of the skin (cream)

dosage.d: Apply 5% lacquer to affected nails once or twice weekly
dosage.t: After filing and cleaning the nail; continue until the nail regrows and is cured (fingernails about 6 months, toenails 9-12 months)
dosage.n: File down the infected nail before the first application and as needed thereafter

dosage.d: Apply 0.25% cream to affected skin once daily
dosage.t: Continue for several days after lesions clear

admin: File down the affected nail (including the surface) and clean with the supplied swab before each application
Apply the lacquer evenly over the whole nail surface and allow to dry (about 3-5 minutes)
Do not apply nail cosmetics or artificial nails during treatment; remove lacquer with the swab before re-filing and reapplying
Avoid contact with the surrounding skin, eyes, ears, and mucous membranes
Continue treatment uninterrupted until a healthy nail has regrown
moa: Amorolfine is a morpholine antifungal that interferes with fungal cell membrane sterol biosynthesis. It inhibits the enzymes delta-14 reductase and delta-7,8 isomerase, depleting ergosterol and causing accumulation of abnormal sterols in the fungal membrane. This disrupts membrane integrity and function, producing fungistatic and fungicidal effects against dermatophytes, yeasts, and some moulds.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to amorolfine or any excipient
relative: Diabetes mellitus or peripheral circulatory disorders affecting the nails (use under medical advice)
monitor: Clinical appearance of the nail and surrounding skin

preg: There are limited data on amorolfine in pregnancy. Systemic absorption from the nail lacquer is negligible, but as a precaution avoid use during pregnancy unless considered necessary.
lact: It is not known whether amorolfine is excreted in human milk; systemic exposure is negligible. As a precaution, avoid use during breastfeeding unless clearly needed.
renal: No dosage adjustment is needed in renal impairment because systemic absorption from topical use is negligible.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is needed in hepatic impairment because systemic absorption from topical use is negligible.

minor: No clinically significant systemic drug interactions are expected because of negligible absorption
interactions.diagnostics: No known interference with laboratory tests

common: Nail disorders (discoloration, brittle or broken nails)
Mild burning sensation of the skin around the nail
rare: Erythema, itching, or blistering of periungual skin
emergency: Severe allergic reaction with swelling or difficulty breathing (very rare) - seek emergency care

monitoring: Clinical and, if needed, mycological response of the treated nail over months
Local skin reactions around the nail
Adherence to the prolonged treatment course
counsel: File the affected nail and clean it before applying the lacquer; let it dry fully
Apply once or twice weekly exactly as instructed and keep treating until a clear, healthy nail grows back - this can take many months
Do not use cosmetic nail polish or false nails on treated nails
Avoid getting the lacquer on surrounding skin, eyes, ears, or mouth, and wash organic solvents off promptly
Tell your doctor if you have diabetes or poor circulation before treating a nail infection yourself
pk: Acts locally in the nail; clinical improvement over weeks to months
Not applicable systemically; persists in the nail plate between applications
Maintains antifungal concentration in the nail for days, allowing once/twice-weekly dosing
Store below 25 C; keep tightly closed and away from heat and flame (flammable solvent)
pearls: Not FDA-approved; information reflects EMA/SmPC and BNF sources
Best suited to mild distal onychomycosis not involving the nail matrix (lunula) and affecting up to two nails
Negligible systemic absorption, so it lacks the systemic interactions of oral antifungals
Treatment is long - file the nail, apply once/twice weekly, and continue until a healthy nail regrows
Consider oral antifungal therapy or specialist referral for matrix involvement or extensive disease
missed: If you forget an application, apply the lacquer as soon as you remember, then continue with your usual once- or twice-weekly schedule. Do not apply extra to make up for a missed application.
overdose: Overdose is very unlikely with topical use. Accidental ingestion of the lacquer may cause local irritation; treat symptomatically and seek advice from a poison control center. Avoid inducing vomiting if the solvent has been swallowed.
